steps: Codes & location

Install to the current CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or ANSI Z223.1 (USA) and local codes, by qualified personnel — only a licensed Plumber and Gas Fitter in Massachusetts. Plan the unit, vent and gas routes together; keep the unit out of high-traffic areas and away from furniture and draperies.

Installation and venting must conform to the current CAN/CGA-B149 installation code (Canada) or the current National Fuel Gas Code, ANSI Z223.1 (USA), and be approved per local codes. Only qualified (licensed or trained) personnel should install it; in Massachusetts, only a licensed Plumber and Gas Fitter.

  • Decide the unit location, the vent system and the gas piping route together: into an existing wall, a corner, a built-in wall or a wall projection (Figure 8).
  • Manufactured (mobile) homes: in some jurisdictions after the "first sale" (consult local codes). The fireplace must be fastened in place. Follow CAN/CSA Z240 MH (Canada), or Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 or ANSI/NFPA 501A (USA).
  • Suitable for a bedroom or bed sitting room.
  • Must not be connected to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance.
Massachusetts (248 CMR 5.08, p. 4): where a side wall vent terminates less than seven (7) feet above finished grade, a hard-wired CO detector with alarm and battery back-up is required on the floor level of the appliance, a CO detector with alarm on each additional level, and a metal or plastic plate reading "GAS VENT DIRECTLY BELOW. KEEP CLEAR OF ALL OBSTRUCTIONS" at least eight (8) feet above grade in line with the terminal.
Position & standoffs
Place the fireplace, then install the top and side standoffs (shipped loose inside it) once it is on site and in position. The safety screen and door frame lift off for access.

The standoffs are shipped loose inside the fireplace and go on the top and the side (Figure 7) once the fireplace is on site and in position. Hold the clearances in Figures 2 and 3 (p. 5).

Door frame removal (p. 6)

  1. Turn off the fireplace and allow ample time for it to cool. The ceramic glass is very fragile.
  2. Remove the safety barrier screen: pry the top toward you, then lift it from its tabs at the base of the door frame. Remove the TC Finishing Touch Trim Kit if installed.
  3. With a screwdriver, push against the notch in the top of the latch, grab the bottom of the latch handle as it protrudes and lift until the latch hook disengages. Repeat on the other side while holding the glass so it does not tip out.
  4. Tilt the top of the frame out to clear the unit, then lift it up and out of its bottom track. Store it safely.
  5. Reassemble in reverse; the latch handle snaps flush with the frame. To check, pull the top left and right of the glass frame forward under moderate pressure: it should return evenly on both sides.
Steel stud framing kit

Frame with the fireplace in place and venting installed. Assemble the supplied kit with every narrow-side hole facing the rear, bend the tabs out 90°, attach the frame to the fireplace and secure it through the tabs to the wood framing.

• Lay the parts on their narrow end on a large flat surface, holes facing up. Top upper/lower stud (#4) horizontal; two center studs (#6) about 8" either side of its center point; inner cross brace (#5) along their bottom ends.
  • Side studs (#2) at each end; lower cross brace (#7) between them about 6" from their lower ends, narrow vertical side facing outward.
  • Two framing plates (#8) on the outside of each side stud: 16 inches from the top of the lower plate to the top of the upper plate, holes toward the rear, lined up with the framing brackets on the fireplace.
  • Outer side studs (#3) tab side out, then the second upper/lower stud (#4) at the bottom. Join the parts with the supplied wafer screws (#1).

The lintel is fixed: maneuver the fireplace so the front face of the lintel sets its final position, allowing for the facing thickness. The kit gives a 1 7/8 inch adjustment along the framing brackets. Sheet metal parts have sharp edges.
Board, facing & hearth

Sheet the front with non-combustible board 11 7/8" above and 10 1/8" to the sides of the framing edges, fixed with #8 drywall screws. Facing must not stop the door or screen from opening; keep any hearth no more than 1" above the bottom of the fireplace.

• Board: cement board or equivalent; standard drywall may be used beyond it. Calcium silicate board is 1/2" thick: pre-drill the mounting holes, handle it with care and don't use it if cracked.
  • Recessed: masonry type non-combustible material up to 4 1/2" proud of the appliance; deeper, move the facing away from the unit and window, top and sides, at 1:1, up to a maximum 12" deep (Figure 11).
  • Painted wall above: discard the framing kit and use full sheets of calcium silicate board and full-length metal studs.
  • A hearth extension is not required. If one is thicker than 1", raise the fireplace accordingly; thicker hearths interfere with the safety screen and door frame.

For a flush finish the fireplace accommodates facing from 1/2" to 2 1/4" thick (p. 14), using the framing kit's 1 7/8" adjustment along the framing brackets (p. 13); a 3/4" facing finishes flush with the front of the unit (p. 8).
Electrical & wall switch

Connect 110 V. AC to the junction box behind the right-side firebox access panel. Mount the wall switch, run the supplied 40 ft. cable to the interface board (check its continuity before walling in), fit the 4 "AA" batteries and set NV or PV.

1. With the fireplace in place, remove the door and the access panel on the right-hand side of the firebox.
  2. Connect the 110 V. AC supply to the wires inside the junction box (fireplace rated 110 volts, 60Hz, 0.25A).
  3. Attach the wall switch to the framing, route the supplied control cable, and connect one end to the wall control and the other to the interface board.
  4. Insert the 4 supplied "AA" batteries into the wall switch battery pack.
  5. If not already installed, install the burner using the instructions supplied with the burner kit.
  6. Turn on the gas, check that all connections are tight and leak free, then turn on gas and electrical supplies.

Check the continuity of each wire in the communication cable before it is plugged in at both ends and walled in. Set the NV / PV switch on the interface board: NV without a power vent, PV with one. When switching, turn off the power supply and remove the backup batteries to reset the module.
Gas connection & pressure check

Bring the line through the control box access holes to the 3/8" N.P.T. valve inlet with a union or flare fitting (don't hard pipe) and a sediment trap within 6 feet; leak-test. Verify pressures with the fireplace lit on its highest setting.

• Gas supply access holes are at the top and left sides of the control box. Use the correct gas line diameter for proper operation and pressure.
  • Sediment trap per the national fuel gas code, no more than 6 feet from the gas control valve.
  • Connect the supply to the valve (Figure 26), turn on the gas and check that all connections are tight and leak free.
  • Testing the supply piping: disconnect the appliance and its shut off valve above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); isolate it by closing its manual shut off valve at or below 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa).
  • Turn off the gas before removing a test-port plug. Supply: 5.0" – 13.9" WC natural gas, 12.5" – 13.9" WC propane. Manifold: 1.6" – 3.5" WC natural gas, 6.4" – 10" WC propane. The test procedure is in the separate Burner Installation Manual.
Reinstall the access panel, including its gasket, after installation, conversion or servicing. Without it the control system overheats and fails prematurely.
Venting & termination

Use the Town & Country wall (22270012) or roof (22270010) termination kit within the Figure 38 / 39 rise-run charts (68 feet total max), with a 1/4" rise per 1 ft. of horizontal run and 1 3/4" to combustibles. Screw every joint and tape the outer joints.

Wall termination

  • Minimum 4 foot of pipe off the top of the fireplace (48" pipe 22220010 before the first elbow); with a 90° elbow, up to 20 ft. of horizontal run.
  • Cut and frame a 14 1/2" opening (round or square) centered at least 84 1/2" above the floor, higher as the horizontal run increases. Walls up to 12" thick.
  • Trim the wall thimble/shield to the wall thickness (siding included) so it sits flush outside. Fully engage both pipes in the terminal; it must not be recessed into the wall or siding. Caulk it in place.

Roof termination

  • Frame a 14 1/2" opening in each floor, ceiling or roof (larger as roof pitch increases, Figure 40); avoid cutting rafters.
  • Ceiling firestop (TCVT.THIMA) at each floor or ceiling. Into an attic, leave its shield full length and add a storm collar on top; an Attic Insulation Shield (SKU #22270029) may be required.
  • The pipe must extend at least 12" above the roof (more on steeper roofs). Fit the roof support bracket, flashing, storm collar with a ring of mastic, then the cap; seal screw heads and joints with caulking.

Hold the Figure 43 terminal clearances (p. 28).
Vent restrictor

Set the vent restrictor on the underside of the firebox top (it leaves the factory open) from the Figure 46 rise/run chart, then fine-tune by flame appearance. It must be fully open with the TCVT.PVB1 power vent kit.

Determine the vent height and the horizontal length, read the restrictor position from the chart (Figure 46), then loosen the screw, move the restrictor to its opening and re-tighten. Positions are based on lab tests; the ideal position may vary slightly with the installation.

Too closedflame excessively tall and lifting · lacks movement · soots
Too openflame height low · excessive movement
Firebox panels & burner

Remove the side panel retainers and move the restrictor plates out, then fit the back panel, side panels, retainers, burner tray (screwed down) and the front panel. Install the burner per the burner kit's instructions.

1. Remove the side panel retainers on the underside of the firebox heat shield (one screw each).
  2. Move the restrictor plates out so the top of the back panel clears the tabs as it tilts in.
  3. Insert the back panel, tabs down, into the right and left tab supports.
  4. Supporting the back panel, set each side panel: rear end on the side panel supports, front end on the horizontal support.
  5. Reinstall the side retainers; install the burner tray and secure it with the provided screws.
  6. Rest the front panel over the horizontal support, long vertical edge toward the front. It is not fastened with screws.

Valve service (p. 36): remove the front panel base (and the rear panel base if a Black Diamond Burner is fitted), all media (sand or glass), the burner tray, the right side panel retaining clip and side panel, then the access panel. Reassemble in reverse.
Trim, screen & pairing
Fit the transition trim kit (SKU #80002247) and the magnetic safety barrier screen, then link the wall switch to the fireplace and the remote handset to the wall switch.

• Trim, with the door in place: the two side pieces first (two smaller magnets each), then the top piece over them (two larger magnets). The meshed bottom piece rests on the floor in the gap between the outer-most door frame and the glass; fix the Town & Country badge to its right-hand side.
  • Attach the magnetic safety barrier screen to the outer-most door frame.
  • Wall switch to fireplace: selector on "Remote", press and hold the Program button (straightened paper clip) for up to 10 seconds; release after 5 beeps. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then 3 more.
  • Remote to wall switch: press and release Program once (3 beeps), then the remote's on/off button within 60 sec.; 3 beeps confirm. If another nearby fireplace responds, repeat the first procedure to move to another of three channels.
Leave the manuals with the appliance.

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace has an ignition device that lights the pilot automatically. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Everyday start

Press ON/OFF on the remote. The fireplace beeps once to confirm. The pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light each time you turn it on. Then set the flame with the remote.

Full lighting steps

  1. Stop and read the safety information first (see Safety & gas smell). Smell all around the fireplace for gas, including next to the floor.
  2. Push the On/Off switch to turn the fireplace on. If the burner lights, go to step 5.
  3. If it doesn't light, push the On/Off switch to off.
  4. Wait at least 5 minutes for any gas inside to clear. If you still smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps. If you don't, go back to step 2.
  5. Set the fireplace the way you want it with the hand-held remote.

Lighting it for the first time? Allow time for air to escape from the gas lines.

Won't light or stay lit after several tries? Push the On/Off switch to off, turn off all electric power to the fireplace, and call your service technician or gas supplier.

Turning it off

Push the On/Off switch to off. For service or a long shutdown, also turn off all electric power and remove the backup batteries. The main on/off switch is on the wall switch.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
Your Proflame 2 remote has an ON/OFF key, a THERMOSTAT key, up and down arrow keys, a MODE key and a blue back-lit screen. It runs on 3 AAA batteries.

  • On and off: press ON/OFF. The fireplace beeps once to confirm. When it's off, the screen shows only the room temperature.
  • Flame height: there are six flame levels. Each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one step, until the flame is off. The up arrow raises it. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, the up arrow brings the flame back on high.
  • Light: press MODE until the light bulb icon shows, then use the arrows to pick one of six levels.
  • Key lock: press MODE and the up arrow together to lock the keys. A lock icon appears. Press them together again to unlock.
  • °F or °C: with the remote off, press THERMOSTAT and MODE together, then check that a C or F shows next to the room temperature.
Thermostat key: the thermostat function is disabled by default. The manual says thermostat use is not permissible in the USA but is permissible in Canada. The Canadian steps to turn it on are on page 9 of the owner's manual.

If the remote's batteries are low or dead, turn the fireplace off with the ON/OFF switch on the wall switch.

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
A smell the first few hours

The first time you light it, the fireplace gives off a slight odor for a couple of hours. That's the paints, sealants and lubricants used in manufacturing as they cure. It's temporary. Open doors and windows to air out the room. The odor may bother some people.

Ticking and creaking

Steel fireplaces make some expansion and contraction noises as they start up and cool down. You hear the same kind of thing from a furnace or an oven. It's normal.

Beeps

  • One beep after you press a remote key means the fireplace got the command.
  • A double beep means the backup batteries are low. Replace them (see Power & batteries).

A short wait

The pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light each time you turn the fireplace on.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch electrical switches and don't use any phone in your building. Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbour's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass whenever it needs it, using fireplace glass cleaner.

  • Only when it's cool. Never clean the glass while it's hot. Hot glass causes burns, so don't touch it until it has cooled.
  • No abrasive cleaners on the glass or on any other part of the fireplace.
  • Clean the outside finish with mild soap and water.

The safety screen

A screen barrier comes with your fireplace to reduce the risk of burns from the hot glass. To take it off, pull the top of the screen toward you, then lift it off its tabs at the bottom of the door frame. Always put it back before you use the fireplace.

Cracked or broken glass

Don't strike the glass or knock anything against it. Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken. A licensed or qualified service person should replace it, with ceramic glass only (38" x 14" x 5mm) from a Town & Country dealer.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
modes.html:
Your fireplace's control module lights the pilot automatically and keeps watch on the pilot flame. It offers two pilot modes:

IPIintermittent pilot ignition
CPIcontinuous pilot ignition

Switching modes

  1. Turn the system off.
  2. Press MODE until the CPI icon shows on the remote's screen.
  3. Press the up arrow to choose CPI, or the down arrow to go back to IPI.
  4. One beep from the fireplace confirms the change.

In either mode, never try to light the pilot by hand. Each time you turn the fireplace on, the pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light.

At the yearly inspection, your service person checks the pilot's flame size and operation and cleans it.

power.title: Power & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace's control runs on house power, with a backup battery pack.

Backup batteries4 "AA", in the wall switch battery pack
Remote3 AAA

In a power outage

The backup batteries power the control only when house power is interrupted or lost, and only if the fireplace doesn't use a combustion fan. Battery power is for temporary, short-term use.

Low-battery signs

  • Remote: a battery icon appears on the screen before the power runs out. It goes away once you put in new batteries. Meanwhile, you can turn the fireplace off with the ON/OFF switch on the wall switch.
  • Backup batteries: the fireplace gives a double beep when it gets a command from the remote. After you replace them, it beeps once again.

Battery life depends on battery quality, how often the fireplace lights and how often the thermostat setting is changed.

Changing batteries: the installation manual says to turn off the main gas supply to the fireplace before removing or reinserting the batteries. For service or a long shutdown, also turn off all electric power and remove the backup batteries.

pair.title: Pairing the remote and the app
pair.html:
The remote works through the wall switch, so pairing has two steps: wall switch to fireplace, then remote to wall switch.

1. Wall switch to fireplace

  1. Set the wall switch selector to Remote.
  2. Press and hold the Program button for up to 10 seconds. Use a straightened paper clip to reach it.
  3. Let go after the wall switch beeps 5 times. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then 3 more. They're paired.

2. Remote to wall switch

  1. Press and release the Program button once. The wall switch beeps 3 times.
  2. Within 60 sec., press and release ON/OFF on the remote. Three beeps from the wall switch mean it's paired.

TC Fire app (optional)

Get the free TC Fire app from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store. Go to Add/Edit Fireplace, press Add, enter the PIN from the sticker on the wall switch and a name, then press Save. The app turns the flame and the light on and off and sets their levels. Your fireplace only shows when your phone is within Bluetooth range and no one else is controlling it.

If a nearby fireplace turns on instead of yours, repeat step 1 to switch to another of three channels. With a home automation system, leave the wall switch on Remote.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbour's phone, and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell all around the fireplace, including next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles there.

Hot glass and children

Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. The barrier screen that comes with the fireplace reduces the risk of burns and must be installed to protect children and other at-risk people. Supervise young children in the same room. If anyone at risk lives in the house, a physical barrier is recommended, and an adjustable safety gate can keep them out of the room.

Around the fireplace

  • Keep clothing, furniture, draperies and other flammable material away.
  • Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids near it.
  • Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician right away to inspect the fireplace and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
  • Put back any panel, grill or door removed for service before you use it.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have a qualified service person inspect the fireplace and its venting before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpets or bedding can mean more frequent cleaning. The control compartments, burners and air passageways must be kept clean.

The yearly inspection

  1. Remove the glass and check the decorative media (logs, pebbles, glass and so on) for soot. Heavy soot means the unit needs inspecting and adjusting for proper combustion. The media and burner are cleaned, with close attention to the burner ports.
  2. Check the pilot for proper flame size and operation, and clean it.
  3. Check that the vent pipe and vent terminal are open and free of blockage or debris.
  4. Check the glass gasket and replace it if needed. A good glass seal matters.
  5. Check the batteries and replace them as needed.
Don't repair it yourself. If you find a problem, contact your dealer to have it repaired. Before any service, the gas and electrical power are turned off and the fireplace is left to cool.

Keep the area around the fireplace clear of combustible materials, gasoline and other flammable vapours and liquids.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Town & Country's limited lifetime warranty for gas products covers the original registered purchaser.

Glass (thermal breakage only), combustion chamber, burner tube assembly, porcelain finishesLimited lifetime, parts only
Any defective part2 years, parts and labor, from the original date of purchase

Conditions

  • Installed by a qualified technician to local and national requirements and the appliance manual.
  • Sediment traps installed within 6 feet of the gas control valve.
  • The installer makes sure it fires as per the rating plate.
  • Porcelain is warranted for gloss retention. Some colors darken when heated and return to their shade when cool, and minor imperfections can occur.

Not covered

  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident or lack of maintenance.
  • Mantels, surrounds or finishing material around the fireplace.
  • Installation, operational or environmental conditions beyond Town & Country's control.
Any installation or operating deviation from the manual's instructions voids the warranty. This is a summary; the full terms are in the owner's manual.

Don't hard pipe the line to the valve: provide a union or flare fitting to allow repair or replacement of the gas valve. Disconnect the appliance and its shut off valve during supply-piping tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); close its manual shut off valve for tests at or below 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa).

Max total vent length68 feet (wall and roof charts)

Rise and run must stay inside the Figure 38 (wall, p. 24) and Figure 39 (roof, p. 25) charts; keep the vent length and the number of elbows to a minimum and support the pipe. Screw every joint and seal all outer joints with the supplied high-temperature self-adhesive aluminum tape; the inner pipe needs no sealing. A wall thimble/shield is required through a combustible wall and a ceiling firestop (TCVT.THIMA) through a floor or ceiling.

Approved components (p. 22): pipe 12" 22220006, 18" 22220007, 24" 22220008, 48" 22220010, 12" adjustable 22220005; 45° elbow 22220009; 90° elbow 22220011; wall/offset support 22220012; wall shield/ceiling firestop 22270011; roof flashing adjustable 22220002, flat 22220003, steep 22220004, or any flashing that fits 11" pipe.

Never connect to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance.

Page 5 refers to Figure 2, the mantel clearance chart (clearance and mantel depth, measured from the top of the lintel bar); its values are tied to lettered dimensions in the drawing, so read them there.

The unit may be recessed up to 4 1/2" with non-combustible masonry type material. A hearth extension is not required and combustible flooring may run up to the fireplace, but many materials (such as wood flooring) may not tolerate the radiant heat; a non-combustible hearth no more than 1" above the bottom of the fireplace is suggested. Keep the fireplace out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies.

specFrame.title: Framing & facing
specFrame.html:
The supplied Steel Stud Framing Kit (80001418) must be used unless the fireplace is totally enclosed with non-combustible material such as facing brick. Frame with the fireplace in place and venting installed. Sides, back and top can be framed with conventional lumber up to the steel studs and standoffs; a full header above the framing kit is highly recommended.

No combustible material, electrical wiring, insulation, plastic vapor barrier or gas plumbing within the steel stud framing.
Non-combustible backer board (cement board or equivalent)11 7/8" above and 10 1/8" to the sides of the framing edges
Facing thickness, flush install1/2" to 2 1/4" (p. 14)
Masonry non-combustible proud of the applianceup to 4 1/2"
Deeper recessfacing set back 1:1, top and sides, to a maximum 12" deep
Framing bracket adjustment1 7/8"
Calcium silicate board1/2" thick

For a flush finish the fireplace accommodates facing from 1/2" to 2 1/4" thick (p. 14), using the framing kit's 1 7/8" adjustment along the framing brackets (p. 13); a 3/4" facing finishes flush with the front of the unit (p. 8).

Standard drywall may be used beyond the board. If the board won't be finished with tile or other non-combustible material, make its top sections a single sheet of calcium silicate board; taped and mudded joints may crack. If the wall above will be painted, discard the framing kit and use full sheets of calcium silicate board and full-length metal studs. The lintel is fixed, so its front face sets the fireplace's final position. Facing must not interfere with the door or screen opening.

Chase: insulate the outer walls to the same degree as other exterior walls, cover insulation and vapour barrier with drywall, don't place the fireplace against insulation, and seal the chase at the ceiling level or between floors. The minimum combustible framing dimensions are a drawing (Figure 13, p. 9).

specElec.title: Electrical & controls
specElec.html:
Fireplace110 volts, 60Hz, 0.25A
Optional power vent kit115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A
Communication cable to the wall switch40 ft. (supplied)
Backup batteries4 "AA" (supplied), wall switch battery pack
Remote transmitter3 AAA

Connect the 110 V. AC supply to the wires in the junction box behind the access panel on the right-hand side of the firebox; the wires can be reached from inside or outside the box through either small access panel. Check the continuity of each wire in the communication cable before it is walled in. For installation or maintenance, turn the fireplace off at the wall on/off switch and at its power supply circuit breaker, and turn off the main gas supply while working on the receiver/module.

NV / PV switch (interface board): NV without a power vent, PV with one. When switching, turn off the power supply and remove the backup batteries to reset the module.

Home automation: flame and light on/off through a dry contact relay; flame and light level through a 0 - 10 volt DC analog signal (Low = 1 volt, High = 10 volts). The control repeats a signal every 2 hours or until a new command arrives. Two cables: the top one from the wall switch to the fireplace, the bottom one to the home automation system. Leave the wall switch on Remote.

Note: p. 16 rates the optional power vent kit at 115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A; the rating label on p. 45 lists a blower electrical rating of 115v, 60hz, 1.1 A right after the power vent kits. The manuals describe no other blower.

Flush facing thickness: p. 8 says a facing thickness of 3/4" allows the finishing surface to be flush with the front of the unit; p. 14 says flush installs accommodate facing from 1/2" to 2 1/4" thick (with the fixed lintel and 1 7/8" framing-bracket adjustment, p. 13). Shown in the Framing & facing spec drawer and the 'Board, facing & hearth' install step.
conflicts.reason: On a second read both fit: p. 14 gives the range of facing thickness the fireplace accommodates for a flush finish (1/2" to 2 1/4", set with the framing kit's 1 7/8" bracket adjustment, p. 13), and p. 8's 3/4" is one thickness inside that range that finishes flush. The drawer and the install step now state both together, without a box. (Figure 13, p. 9, also prints "RANGE 1/2" - 2 1/2"" beside "FRAMING LINTEL" in the minimum combustible framing drawing; what it measures shows only in the drawing, so it is not transcribed.)

review.notes: Installation Manual pages 46-47 and Owner's Manual page 19 are blank. The input rates, efficiency (P.4.1-15 38.4%, a single figure with no NG/LP split), altitude (0 - 4500 ft.) and certification appear only on the rating label (p. 45); the label lists no manifold minimums, so those come from the p. 20 table. No conversion kit part number appears in either manual (only "not convertible ... unless a certified kit is used"), so the guide has no fuel-conversion card. The gas pressure test procedure and the burner/media installation are in a separate Burner Installation Manual (pp. 16, 20) that isn't one of this guide's manuals. Neither manual has a troubleshooting chart or an LED/code table: the fault panels come from the vent restrictor flame descriptions (p. 30), the lighting-failure instruction (Owner p. 4), the battery, pairing and channel notes (Owner pp. 8, 10, 11; Install p. 39) and the annual-inspection soot and glass warnings (p. 41); codes is empty and beeps are described in the drawers. Not transcribed because the values live only in drawings: Figure 1 appliance dimensions (p. 5: 57 15/16", 48 7/16", 45 1/16", 24 7/8"... unlabelled, so H/W/D can't be assigned), the Figure 2 mantel chart (p. 5: lettered clearances A-C 9"/6"/3" and depths D-F 12"/6 3/4"/1 1/2"; the pairing is only in the drawing, so the guide gives the label's 9 in. mantel-to-appliance and 12 in. maximum extension and points to Figure 2), Figures 9 and 13 framing dimensions (pp. 8-9), the Figure 40 roof-opening A/B sizes by pitch (p. 26), the Figure 44 adjacent-structure clearances (p. 29), the Figure 46 restrictor rise/run chart (p. 30) and the Figure 51/53 pipe dimensions and offsets (pp. 32-33). Thermostat: the Owner's Manual notice (p. 6) says the thermostat function is disabled by default and not permissible in the USA (permissible in Canada); the LCD legend ties THERMOSTAT OFF/ON/SMART to that notice, so the guide doesn't present the Smart or room thermostat as usable in the US. The Owner's Manual's generic Proflame 2 text mentions a six-speed comfort fan (p. 7) and the label a blower rating, but neither manual describes a fan or blower for this model, so there is no blower tile. Battery location: the Installation Manual puts the 4 AA backup batteries in the wall switch battery pack (p. 16); the Owner's Manual calls them the IFC module (receiver) batteries (p. 10). The Install p. 2 instruction to turn off the main gas supply before removing or reinserting "the batteries" sits in a receiver/module notice; the guide quotes it as written. Install p. 17 refers to a "Bluetooth Wall Switch" and a "Basic Wall Switch" (Figure 30); neither manual says which one ships with the fireplace or whether the TC Fire app needs the Bluetooth one, so the guide describes the app as the Owner's Manual does (PIN sticker on the wall switch). Naming: the Installation Manual cover says Series D2, the Owner's Manual cover and rating label say Series D ("TCWS38D - Version 2"). Cross-reference slips in the Installation Manual: p. 17 says linking is on "page 39 (Bluetooth Wall Switch) and page 40 (Basic Wall Switch)" but pp. 39-40 are steps 1 and 2 of one procedure; p. 23 cites "Figure 432" (Figure 43); p. 26 says "See Figure 40 for precise lengths" of pipe above the roof, but the roof-pitch heights are the Figure 44 table (p. 29). Part-number notes (not used in the guide unless stated): power vents appear as 22270003, 22270004 & 22270013 (p. 21), TCVT.PVB1 (p. 30) and TCVT.PVI.25 / TCVT.PV7.110 / TCVT.PVCV / TCVT.PVVT (label, p. 45), not reconciled; p. 44 lists the halogen light assembly 80000556 and bulb 80002650 and also "#7 Lights, Part #80001810 esch."; the wall shield/ceiling firestop 22270011 is labelled "OPTIONAL" in Figures 48-49 (p. 31), while pp. 22 and 26 say a wall thimble/shield or ceiling firestop must be used through combustible walls, floors and ceilings (the guide states the requirement). Page 6 describes the safety screen as lifting off tabs at the base of the door frame and p. 38 as a magnetic screen attached to the outer-most door frame; both are given. Catalog fields not checkable against the manual: view_area 478 sq in (the only glass size is the 38" x 14" x 5mm replacement glass, p. 41) and the feature claim of power venting up to 110 ft (not stated in the manuals). check_numbers: every number in the guide was found in the manual text (the label's NG minimum 31,000 is the only input figure that differs from the catalog). The lighting label (Owner p. 4, item C) carries a line about pushing in or turning the gas control knob by hand only, never with tools, and not repairing a knob that won't move (force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion); the lighting steps use the On/Off switch and the remote and neither manual describes a knob procedure, so the guide gives that line in the Safety drawer as printed and adds no knob steps of its own. The Safety drawer's under-water warning follows the manual's full wording (Install p. 3, Owner pp. 3-4), including replacing any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
